sections.label: The opening
sections.line: To create one repository and one DNS record, the site factory's pipeline holds power over the whole organisation.
sections.para: Pipelines now need behaviour policies, like agents.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: A small job, a large grant, no scale limits, changing code, and a policy for the pipeline.

sections.label: A simple job, a large grant
sections.line: The GitHub App token covers every repository: administration, contents and workflows, including delete.
sections.para: No long-lived keys, but far more power than the job needs.

sections.label: Why five hundred repositories?
sections.line: Nothing limits how many repositories or DNS records; the role may point any subdomain anywhere.
sections.para: IAM can limit names and types, not targets.

sections.label: Why we used to get away with it
sections.line: We got away with it because pipeline code did not change; here requests arrive as pull requests.
sections.para: A merged change to the workflow would inherit the whole grant.

sections.label: A behaviour policy for a pipeline
sections.line: Each capability with a reach, an undo class, a limit and a boundary outside the grant.
sections.para: Brokers, narrowed tokens, and protection on .github/.

sections.label: Why this matters beyond one factory
sections.line: Agents now drive pipelines; the credentials did not shrink and the code stopped being fixed.
sections.para: The gap RiskMandate exists to close.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Nothing exploited; reviewer and branch settings unchecked; the limits are proposals.
